Remote desktop to a cloud Mac mini: Remote Screen, SSH, Screen Sharing

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

A WodeMac cloud Mac is delivered with the WodeMac Remote Screen app, which opens the full desktop from a computer, phone or iPad, and WodeMac helps you with the first login. SSH (Remote Login) and Screen Sharing are built-in macOS features, not connection methods promised at delivery. With admin rights you can turn them on in System Settings if you need them, after confirming they can be reached from your network. For everyday work the remote screen is enough; consider SSH when most of your work is in a terminal.

The three options

  • WodeMac Remote Screen: preinstalled at delivery. It opens the full graphical desktop of the Mac from a computer, phone or iPad, which suits everyday development, Xcode and other graphical apps.
  • SSH (macOS Remote Login): command line only and light on bandwidth, good for scripts, Git and long jobs in tmux.
  • Screen Sharing: the remote desktop built into macOS, usually opened from another Mac with its Screen Sharing app.

The last two are macOS system features. They are not guaranteed to be on at delivery, or reachable from your network.

Start with WodeMac Remote Screen

Delivery is usually within 24 hours of payment and no later than 3 business days. WodeMac helps you remotely with the first login. After that, WodeMac Remote Screen opens the whole desktop: on a computer through the WodeMac Mac app or a browser, on a phone or iPad through a browser.

How smooth it feels depends on the network path from where you are to California. Tell us your region before ordering and we can confirm the connection method. Once connected, Terminal, Xcode and your browser work as they would on a Mac on your desk.

Turning on SSH (Remote Login)

Open System Settings > General > Sharing, turn on Remote Login and allow only the users who need it. Prefer keys to passwords: create a key on your own computer and add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for that user on the cloud Mac.

ssh-keygen -t ed25519          # on your own computer
ssh username@host              # connect
tmux new -s work               # a session you can reattach to later

Whether the SSH port can be reached from outside depends on the hosting network. Contact WodeMac to confirm a working connection method before you rely on it; switching the setting on does not by itself make the Mac reachable.

Screen Sharing and security

Screen Sharing is turned on in the same place, System Settings > General > Sharing, and suits people who already work on another Mac. Reachability needs the same check first. In most cases the preinstalled remote screen already covers graphical work.

  • Turn on only the services you need and allow only the users who need them.
  • Use a strong password for the macOS account and key-based login for SSH.
  • Do not save connection passwords on shared devices.
  • WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access through DeskIn for maintenance. Contact WodeMac before changing remote access settings, so support is still possible if something goes wrong.

FAQ

Is SSH already enabled at delivery?

What is guaranteed at delivery is the preinstalled WodeMac Remote Screen app. SSH (Remote Login) and Screen Sharing are macOS features you can turn on with admin rights; confirm with WodeMac first that they can be reached from your network.

Can I connect from a phone or iPad?

Yes. Open WodeMac Remote Screen in a browser on the phone or iPad to see the full desktop. On a computer you can use the WodeMac Mac app or a browser.

Does a running job stop when the remote desktop disconnects?

No, only the display link drops; the Mac keeps running. Put long jobs in tmux or under launchd so they continue even if a terminal window is closed.

Why does it sometimes lag?

Responsiveness depends on the network path from you to California and on current conditions. Command-line work needs far less bandwidth, so lean on the terminal when the connection is poor.
